author: Amr
subject: ci(quality): add Lighthouse CI + axe/pa11y accessibility checks on PRs
body:
New site-quality.yml builds _site with the build-validation PR config,
serves it locally (gzip, Pages-style URLs) and runs:
- Lighthouse CI on /, /quests/, /quests/0000/hello-noob/ (mobile, 3 runs,
  median): a11y/best-practices/SEO >= 0.95 and must-pass audits at 'error'
  where they pass today; perf, Web Vitals and size budgets at 'warn';
  cache-policy audits off (GitHub Pages max-age=600).
- axe-core via Playwright on 7 key pages at 390px + 1366px: fails on
  critical/serious WCAG 2.0/2.1 A/AA; WCAG 2.2 target-size warns;
  pre-existing issues (quest-objective checkbox labels, theme intro
  share/edit names) warn with a TODO, scoped to their nodes.
- pa11y WCAG 1.4.3 contrast on /notes/, one note and /search/.

Reports: job summary, annotations, site-quality-reports artifact and LHCI
temporary public storage. No AI, no secrets, advisory (not required).

author: claude[bot]
subject: fix(deps): stop committing Gemfile.lock (fleet never-commit policy)
body:
Gemfile.lock was tracked despite .gitignore:16. Dependabot's lockfile-only
bundler PR #751 satisfied a ruby-group bump by downgrading github-pages
232 -> 222 (liquid 4.0.3, which calls String#tainted?, removed in Ruby 3.2),
so ci, Jekyll Build Test and dependabot-auto-merge went red every week.

- git rm --cached Gemfile.lock (the .gitignore rule stays)
- docker-compose.yml comments: the lockfile is local-only, not committed
- AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md: drop the stale "must be committed"
  guidance in favour of the fleet policy

Refs bamr87/bamr87#333

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: claude[bot]
subject: fix(deps): floor github-pages at >= 232 so Bundler cannot walk it back
body:
Verified in ruby:3.4 (the Dockerfile image): with no lockfile and an
unconstrained `gem 'github-pages'`, a fresh `bundle install` still resolves
github-pages 222 / jekyll 3.9.0 / liquid 4.0.3 and `jekyll build` exits 1.
With the floor it resolves github-pages 232 / jekyll 3.10.0 / liquid 4.0.4
and the build passes. A floor is allowed by fleet policy (no pins, no
ceilings).

Refs bamr87/bamr87#333

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: bamr87
subject: content(quests): add Install Windows 11 quest for a laptop with a blank SSD
body:
New Level 0000 main quest that walks a learner through a clean Windows 11
install onto a brand-new SSD: fitting the drive, building install media on
Windows (Media Creation Tool or Rufus), macOS or Linux (wimlib split for
FAT32), UEFI firmware checks, the Setup wizard including the Intel VMD
"We couldn't find any drives" driver fix, first boot (OOBE), and post-install
drivers, activation and BitLocker recovery-key checks.

Illustrated with 11 images from public sources: Microsoft documentation
screenshots used under Microsoft's screenshot guidelines, Wikimedia Commons
photos (CC BY / CC BY-SA) and the Rufus project's own screenshot, each
credited in its caption and in the Image Credits table.

Also lists the quest on the Level 0000 hub, unlocks it from OS Selection,
and regenerates the quest navigation and network data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: bamr87
subject: fix(ui): restore mobile TOC button, space task-list checkboxes, turn on giscus
body:
Mobile TOC: the theme renders the table-of-contents FAB only for a
hard-coded list of its own layouts, so quest, quest-hub, quest-collection,
home-os, notes-workbench and javascript pages had a TOC with no button to
open it below lg. _includes/custom/footer.html (the theme's consumer hook)
renders it for any local layout that extends default, and renders nothing
once the theme emits the FAB itself (bamr87/zer0-mistakes#570).

FAB collision: below lg the local-graph FAB sat on the sidebar FAB's slot
on note pages; user-overrides.css lifts it one slot (zer0-mistakes#571).

Task lists: kramdown checkboxes had no spacing and kept list bullets;
user-overrides.css styles .task-list-item(-checkbox) (zer0-mistakes#573).

giscus: _layouts/quest.html now renders the comments section (same gate as
the theme's article/note layouts); the quests and notes front-matter scopes
set comments: true (the `path: pages` scope never reaches collection
documents); data-repo-id gets its missing base64 padding; the local giscus
fork reads site.giscus.data-theme, set to transparent_dark so the widget
matches the always-dark site (zer0-mistakes#574).

Before/after screenshots in TODO/screenshots/mobile-toc-checkbox-giscus/.
